content: I suggest you first check to see how the messages are being handled by your email provider. That is, are the messages already declared spam or junk when Thunderbird receives them? Email can be classified as spam or junk if the domain is suspicious, the IP address is blacklisted, or the contents of message appear suspicious. No one can explain exactly why your messages are being treated as such. To the possibility that the mail is arriving in Thundebird and not initially marked junk, my suggestion is to start 'training' the junk filter to identify both good and bad mail, not just the bad. More info is at https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/thunderbird-and-junk-spam-messages and also at https://blog.thunderbird.net/2024/09/thunderbird-and-spam/

content:
Hi. First thing to do would be to log off so as not to download any more

Then maybe remove the inbox folder in the current folder to a 'safe' place and then copy across the one you want to see if you have the emails there you want

If all is OK reverse the process and ensure all is OK

There is no 'need' to import a Profile the issue is that the profile that is used is set in the [profiles.ini] file

To be safe copy the file to [profile.inixxx] for example as a backup then edit profile ini to select a different Profile

Effectively if you select another profile via the Thunderbird Gui it will re-write the [profiles.ini]

So check the file etc. to see where it points before you do anything, and always copy the profiles and [profiles.ini] before you fiddle

Read up independently before you try any of the above.

content: From your reply, it seems you're making great progress in this. There is no magic bullet on this stuff. Working with the thunderbird filter will help, but also do check with your email provider, as many have strong filters available that can eliminate some junk before it reaches thunderbird. There are also other products focused on spam that can assist if you're getting hammered with such. I use Mailwasher and it destroys an amazing amount of junk before thunderbird sees it. And this is a war we never win. We just keep fighting. Good luck.
